title: 2025 PAC 90928 FOIA Records

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: 2025 PAC 90928 FOIA Records
communications.communication:
Re:  2025 PAC 90928 FOIA Records

To the FOIA Officer of Winnebago County Sheriff,

This request is made under Illinois Freedom of Information Act. for the following records concerning the request for review designated 2025 PAC 90928 by the Public Access Bureau of the Office of the Attorney General:

1. The underlying FOIA request that is the subject of 2025 PAC 90928, the Sheriff's Office's original written response denying it, and the Sheriff's Office's supplemental response issued after reconsideration.

2. All correspondence between the Sheriff's Office (including the Winnebago County State's Attorney's Office acting on its behalf) and the Public Access Bureau concerning 2025 PAC 90928, from January 1, 2025 to present, including the Bureau's forwarding of the request for review, any response or answer submitted by the Sheriff's Office under 5 ILCS 140/9.5(c), and any closure letter or determination received.

3. All responsive records, including Flock Safety audit logs, produced to the requester in the supplemental response, in the same form and with the same redactions applied in that release.

4. All communications, including emails, letters, and memoranda, sent or received by Winnebago County Sheriff concerning the reconsideration of the original denial, from the date of the original denial to the date of the supplemental response.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If any fees apply, please provide an estimate of the total charges before fulfilling this request. Electronic delivery is the preferred method of receipt.
A response is anticipated within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Thank you for your assistance.
David S. (he/him/his), Lucy Parsons Labs

title: Detroit lien list

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Detroit lien list
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

A list of every property since Jan. 1, 2025 where the City of Detroit placed a lien for failure to pay civil fines in violation of these lines of the city code: 

"If an owner or responsible party does not pay a civil fine or costs assessed pursuant to Subsection (a) of this section, the City may file alien against the property for any unpaid amount in the manner described in Sections 4r(l) and 4r(2) of the Michigan Home Rule City Act, being MCL 117r(n and (2). Nothing in this section shall be interpreted to limit any option otherwise available to the City under law to enforce a iudgment or collect a civil fine."

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

communications.subject: FW: [EXTERNAL] Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Detroit lien list
communications.communication:
This email serves as the City of Detroit’s response to the above-referenced matter. Your request was received at the City of Detroit Law Department Freedom of Information Act Section via facsimile or email on May 27, 2026. Because your request was received by electronic transmission, pursuant to Section 5(1) of the Michigan Freedom of Information Act (the “Act”), MCL 15.235(1); it is deemed to have been received at the Law Department on the next business day, May 28, 2026.

Pursuant to Section 5(2) of the Act, MCL 15.235(2), the City’s response is due within five (5) business days. However, due to the nature and the scope of your request and the volume of the requests received by the City, we are extending the City’s response deadline by ten (10) additional business days in accordance with Section 5(2) (d) of the Act, MCL 15.235(2) (d). Therefore, your request will be granted, denied, or granted in part and denied in part on or before June 18, 2026.

Your request is being handled by Ivars Steins. If you have questions regarding your request, or if you did not provide an email address in your request, please forward it to Ivars Steins at Steinsi@detroitmi.gov<mailto:Steinsi@detroitmi.gov> to provide you a response more readily than by regular mail or fax. Mail and fax are not preferred at this time since they both require in-office support. We thank you in advance for your understanding.

title: Use of force data collection (2017-2025) cities 50-100k (Fairfield Police Department)

communications.subject: Connecticut Freedom of Information Act Request: Use of force data collection (2017-2025) cities 50-100k (Fairfield Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident location, area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

I also request that, if possible and pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(d), fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest and not made for commercial gain. The requested documents will be made available to the public at MuckRock.com.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Samuel Sinyangwe

communications.subject: Fwd: FOIA Request Deletion: NARA-NGC-2020-001128
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader:

Thank you for submitting your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to
the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) via the
*FOIAOnline* website.
We received your request on September 28, 2020.  Your request concerns an
FBI file.

Our office uses the *FOIAonline* portal for FOIA and Privacy Act requests
for the National Archives and Records Administration's *operational* records
(records created by this agency).  Your *FOIAOnline *request is for records
that may be *archival* records (records created by or originated in a
different agency but that may have been transferred to the legal custody of
NARA), to which access is restricted. Therefore, we have forwarded it to
our *Office of Research Services, Special Access and FOIA* (RF) staff who
handle FOIA requests for such archival records.

Since *Research Services* does not process FOIA requests through
*FOIAOnline*, we removed your request from the *FOIAOnline* website.  *Special
Access *staff will assign you a new tracking number, and respond directly
to you. In the future, if you need to follow up with that office directly,
please contact them at the address below, or electronically via email.

The National Archives and Records Administration
Special Access and FOIA Staff (RF)
8601 Adelphi Road, Room 5500
College Park, MD 20740

By phone: 301-837-3190
By fax: 301-837-1864
By email: specialaccess_foia@nara.gov

For your reference, a copy of your request is below.  In the future, please
send all requests for FBI files directly to Special Access and FOIA at
their email address above.

Please visit our website at www.archives.gov/foia for further information
about submitting a FOIA request to NARA.  On our main website,
www.archives.gov, you can learn more about the resources we offer to the
public, and you can access our online catalog.

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and pursuant to guidance received from the
Office of Management and Budget (OMB), federal agencies have adjusted their
normal operations to balance the need of completing its mission-critical
work while also adhering to the recommended social distancing for the
safety of our staff.  As a result of this re-prioritization of activities,
you may experience a delay in receiving a substantive response to your FOIA
request. We apologize for this inconvenience and appreciate your
understanding and patience.

Sincerely,
Susan Gillett
Government Information Specialist
Office of General Counsel
National Archives and Records Administration
College Park, MD 20740-6001
susan.gillett@nara.gov

communications.subject: Re: [21-26886] Freedom of Information Act Request - J Ader
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader,

This is in reply to your Freedom of Information Act request, dated
September 29, 2020 for records relating to Frank Teruggi, Jr., including
FBI case file 100-HQ-474363. Your request was received in this office on
April 8, 2020 and assigned the case number 21-26886.

Your request for FBI records has been referred to our Special Access and
FOIA office. They will provide a separate response.

The National Archives at College Park may also hold a Department of Justice
case file for Teruggi. We hold litigation case files of the *Department of
Justice in Record Group 60: General Records of the Department of Justice*.
These records are arranged into numerical classes based on the infraction
of the law involved, and we have various name indexes that allow us to
locate cases pertaining to specific individuals.

Unfortunately, we cannot conduct a search for these records right now. Due
to the COVID-19 pandemic and pursuant to guidance received from the Office
of Management and Budget (OMB), NARA has adjusted its normal operations to
balance the need of completing its mission-critical work while also
adhering to the recommended social distancing for the safety of our staff.
As a result of this re-prioritization of activities, we are unable to
provide a substantive response to requests that require us to consult the
records at this time. We apologize for this inconvenience and appreciate
your understanding and patience.

We also located responsive records in the Department of State Central File,
1973-1979, which is part of *Record Group 59: General Records of the
Department of State*. The Central File is the primary source for
documentation on U.S. foreign policy and events in various countries.
Documents created between 1974 and 1979 exist in an online database that
contains the telegrams and other correspondence of the Department of State.
Many of these documents are open and available online. You can view the
results of our search, access the documents, and conduct your own searches
here
<https://aad.archives.gov/aad/free-text-search-results.jsp?cat=WR43&bc=sl&q=teruggi&btnSearch=Search&as_alq=&as_anq=&as_epq=&as_woq=>
.

The telegrams are full-text searchable. The P-Reels, which contain
documents other than telegrams, are available in paper at the National
Archives at College Park. The P-Reel indexes are also available online. If
you see P-Reel Index numbers that are of interest to you in the set of
responsive records we linked to above, please let us know so that we may
help you obtain those documents. Documents numbered P80 and later must be
requested through the Department of State.

A helpful guide to the 1973-1979 Central File is located here:
https://www.archives.gov/research/foreign-policy/state-dept/rg-59-central-files/1973-1979.html

We also identified an additional series of responsive State Department
records:

Record Group 59
Records Relating to Horman and Teruggi Litigation, 1961 - 1977
<https://catalog.archives.gov/id/27499859>
Entry UD-14D 86

This series is classified and records in the series need to be reviewed for
categories of information exempted from disclosure under the Freedom of
Information Act (FOIA). We are transferring your request to the National
Declassification Center staff for further action. The National
Declassification Center staff will be in contact about the status of your
request.

If you are searching for records relating to Teruggi's murder by the
Chilean military in the aftermath of the 1973 Chilean coup, many records
related to the coup were declassified and released as part of the Chile
Declassification Project. A searchable database
<https://foia.state.gov/Search/Results.aspx?collection=CHILE&searchText=*> of
these records is available on the State Department's website, and a search
of the database for "Teruggi" yields over 600 hits. The records in the this
database may overlap with some of our holdings, but it is likely that it
also includes material that either has not yet been transferred to us or
that is not available online through the National Archives.

If you have any questions about this database, please contact the
Department of State.

We will continue to process your request when the National Archive resumes
normal operations. For updates on our status, please visit
https://www.archives.gov/coronavirus.

Sincerely,

David Castillo
Archives Specialist
Textual Reference Archives II Branch (RR2RR)
National Archives at College Park, MD

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: The Morris Rd/Hunter Pl Files: Traffic, Transit, and Neighborhood Neglect in SE DC
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO: doee.foia@dc.gov, ddot.foia@dc.gov, foia.synergy@dc.gov

CC: oig_hotline@epa.gov, rwhite@dccouncil.gov, swilson@dccouncil.gov, pmendelson@dccouncil.us, callen@dccouncil.gov, bpinto@dccouncil.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, tkopania@wusa9.com

SUBJECT: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: MS4 Compliance & CIP Exclusions (NPDES Permit DC0000221) for Ward 8 Hazards

To the FOIA Officers and Executive Leadership of D.C. DOEE and DDOT:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally demanding the immediate release of all site-specific compliance documents mandated under the District's National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Master Permit (No. DC0000221) regarding two active Ward 8 hazard sites: 1488-1600 Morris Rd SE and the stagnant pond located at Hunter Place SE.

Timeframe of Requested Records: January 1, 2022, to the date of final search execution.

This request encompasses the following mandatory disclosures:

1. Outfall Inspections & Maintenance Logs:
All maintenance logs, illicit discharge screenings, structural inspections, and repair work orders conducted by DOEE or DC Water for the stormwater outfalls and conveyance systems directly feeding the Hunter Place SE pond and the severed infrastructure at 1490-1600 Morris Rd SE.

2. Stormwater Retention Non-Compliance:
All internal DOEE, DDOT, and DC Water communications regarding MS4 compliance failures, uncontrolled runoff, or topographic collapse at these specific coordinates.

3. Capital Improvement Project (CIP) Exclusions:
Any internal records, memorandums, or funding directives explaining why the failing infrastructure at these two sites was systematically excluded from D.C.'s mandated MS4 annual reporting and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) remediation plans.

4. FEE WAIVER REQUEST:
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees. Disclosure of this information is in the primary public interest to inform District residents, federal environmental regulators, and investigative media at WUSA9 regarding systemic MS4 permit violations in Ward 8. The requester is a community advocate with zero commercial interest in these materials.

If no records exist, indicating a total failure to maintain these federally mandated assets, I expect a formal "no responsive records" declaration by the statutory deadline so that this matter may be fully escalated to the EPA Office of the Inspector General.

Attachments:
https://youtu.be/kOCHrAuwzH0?si=nd2JS2iJaZusBgXa
https://youtu.be/Yu7qfBbI7Fg?si=tlMIr_TIIC9PGlph

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

title: FOIA Request – Acquisitions, Appraisals, and Third-Party Coordination (CRGNSA)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA Request – Acquisitions, Appraisals, and Third-Party Coordination (CRGNSA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Description of Records Requested:

I request copies of the following agency records from the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area (CRGNSA) office and Region 6 Lands & Realty staff, generated between January 1, 2020, and the present date:

1. Appraisal Instructions & Review for "Birkenfeld/Alashik" (Parcel 03090000760000)
- The Request for Appraisal Services (Statement of Work) and Appraisal Instructions sent to the third-party appraiser for the property identified internally as "Birkenfeld" or "Alashik."
- All correspondence regarding the inclusion of a "Hypothetical Condition" or "Extraordinary Assumption" treating the property as General Management Area (GMA) land while it was legally zoned Special Management Area (SMA).
- The Technical Appraisal Review Report (TARR) and any internal "Review Appraiser" notes approving or questioning this zoning assumption.
- Specific Search Target: Emails between Nicole Carver, Holly Chapman, Jen Barnett, or Donna Mickley and Friends of the Columbia Gorge (FOCG) staff (Dan Bell, Kevin Gorman) in December 2024 and February–March 2024.

2. Grant Application "Drafting" & Coordination (LWCF)
- All draft versions of Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) project narratives or proposal forms for the "Mountain Glade," "Cape Horn," or "Birkenfeld" acquisitions, specifically showing "track changes," comments, or edits originating from external email domains ending in @gorgefriends.org.
- All communications regarding the "Threat to Integrity" or "Urgency" scoring criteria for properties already owned by Friends of the Columbia Gorge.
- Specific Search Target: An email dated roughly August 30, 2022, from Dan Bell to Miki Fujikawa/Holly Chapman regarding the removal of the word "required" and insertion of "wiggle room" regarding trail relocations.

3. "Partner-Funded" Appraisals & Financial Agreements
- All Collection Agreements, Reimbursable Agreements, or correspondence authorizing Friends of the Columbia Gorge to pay for, reimburse, or directly contract the federal appraisal for the "Windy Bluff," "Rowena Bluff," or "Birkenfeld" properties.
- All records discussing the use of "escrow fees" or "closing costs" to reimburse FOCG for property taxes incurred during their ownership period (specifically regarding the Rowena Bluff closing in January 2020).

4. Demolition & Environmental Compliance (Catherine Creek/Windy Bluff)
- All internal engineering notes, emails, or "categorical exclusion" documentation regarding the decision to waive physical site visits or Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESA) for the demolition of structures at Catherine Creek (File C24-0002) or Windy Bluff.

Specific Search Target: Emails from Frances Fischer to Jen Barnett in March 2025 regarding "handling this without a site visit."

Search Terms to Apply:
"Birkenfeld", "Alashik", "03090000760000", "Mountain Glade", "Windy Bluff", "Rowena", "Hypothetical Condition", "GMA", "SMA", "Wiggle Room", "Squishiness", "Partner Funded", "Dan Bell", "Renee Tkach".

Fee Category:
I request a waiver of all fees. The disclosure of this information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government—specifically, how federal Land and Water Conservation Funds (LWCF) are valued and prioritized in the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jarrod McClean

communications.subject: Response
communications.communication:
Dear Requestor, 
  
 The City of Azusa is in receipt of your California Public Records Act (“CPRA”) request related to Flock Safety data received on June 11, 2026: 
  
 Under the CPRA, the City’s obligations are to (1) identify the existence of responsive records, (2) determine whether the record or records are disclosable, and (3) if applicable, identify the legal basis for any exemption from disclosure. (See California Government Code, § 7922.540, subds. (a)-(c). The CPRA provides for the inspection or copying of existing identifiable public records; it does not require the City to create records. (See Government Code § 7920.530(a); City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal. 5th 608. 616–627, 629; Haynie v. Superior Court (2001) 26 Cal. 4th 1061, 1075). If information is withheld or redacted, the City need only identify the legal grounds for nondisclosure (Id.) 
  
 The City has (1) identified the existence of responsive records, and (2) has determined that some of these records are disclosable. These records will be produced on a rolling basis. Records, however, which relate to precise location of the City’s ALPR readers are exempt from disclosure under Government Code § 7923.600, subd. (a) because they constitute records revealing law-enforcement security procedures and operational deployment strategies. Disclosure of precise ALPR locations would compromise the effectiveness of the City’s ALPR program by enabling individuals to identify surveillance coverage, avoid detection, exploit coverage gaps, or otherwise undermine law-enforcement operations. The CPRA does not require disclosure of records that would reveal such security procedures or operational vulnerabilities of a local police agency. 
  
 To the extent any portion of the request seeks generalized information about the City’s use of ALPR technology, the City will produce non-exempt, high-level information that does not disclose precise locations or deployment details. Further, some of these records are also exempt from disclosure under the public-interest balancing test set forth in Government Code section 7922.000. Disclosure of precise ALPR camera locations would create a substantial risk to public safety and to the integrity of ongoing and future law-enforcement operations by exposing sensitive surveillance infrastructure and coverage limitations. That risk clearly outweighs any incremental public interest served by disclosure of exact deployment locations. 
  
 The police investigation files exemption encompasses video, audio, and/or other electronic media. Body worn camera video, like any other audio, video or other electronic media taken during a law enforcement inquiry is considered evidentiary material. Like any other piece of evidence connected to a law enforcement investigation, it is not subject to disclosure under the CPRA. Williams v. Superior Court (1993) 5 Cal.4th 337, 361-362. 
  
 Finally, to the extent responsive documents contain Attorney Client Privilege and or Attorney Work Product information they will be redacted or withheld pursuant to Government Code section 7927.705. 
  
 Preparing these documents for disclosure requires the City to review and redact exempt, private, and/or privileged material. These documents are being prepared for public release on a rolling basis. The City will endeavor to provide you with the first set of responsive documents on or about July 13, 2026. 
  
 Thank you, 
  
 Patricia Tachias 
  
 Police Services Administrator

title: FOIA Request — Five South Six LLC Payment of Village Legal Fees

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: FOIA Request — Five South Six LLC Payment of Village Legal Fees
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq., I request copies of records concerning whether Five South Six LLC has been asked, required, agreed, or otherwise discussed paying or reimbursing the Village of La Grange's legal fees and expenses associated with the lawsuit brought by Jonathan Robinson concerning the development at 112 East Burlington Avenue and 5 6th Avenue.

Please provide records from January 1, 2025 through the date of your search responsive to the following:

Communications between the Village and Five South Six LLC, or their respective representatives, concerning payment, reimbursement, indemnification, or defense of the Village's legal fees or expenses relating to the Robinson lawsuit.
Any requests, demands, notices, tenders of defense, agreements, or other records in which the Village asked or required Five South Six LLC to defend, pay, or reimburse the Village for legal fees or litigation expenses.
Any records showing whether Five South Six LLC has agreed, refused, disputed, or otherwise responded to any request that it pay or reimburse the Village's legal expenses.
Invoices, payment records, reimbursement records, or other financial records sufficient to show whether Five South Six LLC has paid or reimbursed any portion of the Village's legal fees or expenses associated with this lawsuit.
Any non-privileged records reflecting a Village determination or discussion concerning whether Sections 11.C or 11.D of the Development Agreement require or permit Five South Six LLC to pay the Village's legal expenses associated with this lawsuit.

For clarity, the contractual provisions prompting this request are Sections 11.C and 11.D of the Development Agreement for 112 East Burlington Avenue and 5 6th Avenue. Section 11.C provides that the Developer agrees to "hold harmless, indemnify, and, at the election of the Village, defend" the Village against claims connected with the Village's review and approval of the development, issuance of approvals, and development or construction. Section 11.D further provides that the Developer agrees to pay the Village's expenses, "including legal fees and administrative expenses," incurred by the Village in defending against such claims, subject to the provision's limitation concerning the Developer's own acts or omissions.

I am not requesting privileged attorney-client communications or attorney work product. I am requesting the underlying non-privileged records showing whether the Village has invoked, discussed, negotiated, or sought to enforce these contractual provisions with Five South Six LLC.

If responsive records contain exempt material, please provide the reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. 5 ILCS 140/7 provides for disclosure of non-exempt portions of records containing exempt information.

Please provide the records electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Concerned Citizen of La Grange

title: MN LexisNexis Data Sharing (Batch 1) (Belle Plaine Police)

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: MN LexisNexis Data Sharing (Batch 1) (Belle Plaine Police)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

Your agency was identified as sharing data with LexisNexis via the Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) or the Community Crime Map (CCM). LexisNexis sells access to this data via AVCC to 2,400 law enforcement agencies around the U.S., including to ICE, the FBI, and the U.S. Navy. We are working on a story and seek to understand what data your department is sharing with these agencies, and what audits are being conducted on the use of that data and the AVCC/CCM platform. To that end, please provide:

1) Signed/executed "AVCC XML Addendum" that is typically attached to a Schedule A or other contracting documents. This dictates what data your agency is required to share, and who it is shared with. 
2) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with LexisNexis. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. The export should be a .csv or .xlsx file. [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]. Here is an example: https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2026/06/09/Data_Classification_Crime_Results_06042026.xlsx
3) Audit of how your data is used: An audit export of how other agencies are accessing and using your department's data. Timeframe: December 1, 2025 - August 1, 2026. 
4) Audit of your agency's queries: An audit of your agency's queries of the AVCC system, from 1/1/2026 through 2/1/2026. 

Occasionally, if your agency is part of a local consortium, your data may not be shared nationally. If this is the case, please provide a signed "Sub-Agency Addendum" (similar to the AVCC XML Addendum, just reworded for local sharing only) or similar document that shows your agency's data is restricted to neighboring agencies.

Hi Lori,

Thank you for the update - it sounds like the data-sharing with LexisNexis may go through a different product called CommunityCrimeMap. Two things make me think Belle Plaine shares info:
1) On CommunityCrimeMap.com there are recent incidents listed, which indicates LexisNexis has access to local data 
2) While trying to sell Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) to Duluth PD, LexisNexis made a list of 72 MN agencies whose data they have access to within AVCC - including Belle Plaine.  

From my research, by virtue of establishing an interface (link) with LexisNexis for the CommunityCrimeMap, agencies also agree to share details of RMS and/or CAD systems with other agencies. I'd guess that LETG does have some sort of interface with LexisNexis to support CommunityCrimeMaps. This request is focused on documents that show what information is being shared with LexisNexis (and whether you can audit how it's used). The Data Classification Crime Results excel doc I linked in the original request was actually from a CommuintyCrimeMap setup. I hope this helps! I'm happy to give you a call or answer questions if it helps you chase this down. I appreciate you taking the time.  

Thank you!

Best,
Shawn

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: FLOCK HISTORY AUDIT REQUEST FOR GEORGIA NORTHERN JUDICIAL DISTRICT COUNTY SHERIFF’S DEPORTMENTS (Hart County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To all relevant open record personnel: 

Public reports state that this county is using cameras from Flock Safety (a.k.a. "Flock"), the automatic license plate reader (ALPR) company. For the purposes of this request, when I refer to "Flock products," this includes hardware (Flock License Plate Readers (LPRs), Flock Safety Falcons, Flock Video Cameras, Flock Mobile Security Trailers, Flock Gunshot and Audio Detection Devices, Flock Drone as First Responder (DFRs), and Flock Alpha) as well as software (Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Flock FreeForm, Flock Vehicle Fingerprint technology, and the National LPR Network). Source:
https://www.flocksafety.com/products


Therefore, pursuant to Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records (dated September 19, 2026 to the time this request is processed):
1. All contracts, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, payment records, budgetary quotes, and related procurement records involving Flock Safety.

2. All training, instructional, presentation, and guidance materials concerning the use of any Flock Safety product or service, including hardware and software. This includes, but is not limited to:
a) Presentations, videos, audio recordings, scripts, manuals, and training materials;
b) Meeting notes discussing the use of Flock products;
c) Technical or operational explanations of how Flock products function; and
d) Internal or external documents used to explain, train on, or promote the use of Flock products.

3. All policies, procedures, agreements, and legal documents relating to Flock Safety or its products, including terms and conditions, privacy impact assessments, standard operating procedures, use policies, data retention policies, legal opinions, warranties, nondisclosure agreements, memoranda of understanding, liability waivers, insurance agreements, and any other formal or informal agreements.

4. All audit, oversight, or compliance records relating to Flock Safety or its products, including security audits, misuse investigations, and reports submitted to oversight bodies.

5. All records reflecting requests from other law enforcement agencies or private entities for data obtained through Flock products, including but not limited to requests for LPR data.

6. All communications and documents that reference
"Flock" / "Flock Safety," including emails, text messages, PDFs, word processing documents, spreadsheets, presentations, etc.

7. All communications with representatives of Flock Safety (email domain: @flocksafety.com) and any and all reports and data of your audits you have made as an agency yourself or have been subject to by any flock audits. 
Please try to include any other miscellaneous documents that facilitate this municipality's relationship with Flock that don't neatly fall neatly into the above categories.
I am a policy analyst for https://www.shirleyhuman.com/, so the requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. Therefore, I request that any fees are waived. But in the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available. I also respectfully ask that my request is expedited, given the newsworthiness of Flock and its activities.

If you need to contact me, you can reach me at info@ShirleyHuman.com or 706-498-4275. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Hanna Davison

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Community ALPR Audit (Peoria Heights Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

I hereby request the following records: 1. Justification Records All records used to justify adoption of Flock Safety cameras, including but not limited to: staff reports, city council or county board memoranda, crime analysis reports, presentations, vendor proposals, and any other documents that described the purpose, anticipated benefit, or stated rationale for purchasing or leasing the system. 
2. Effectiveness and Use Statistics All statistical reports, internal summaries, use-justification documents, crime-reduction assessments, or after-action reviews evaluating the effectiveness of Flock Safety cameras since installation. This includes any records prepared in connection with contract renewals. 
3. Cost and Financial Records All financial records related to Flock Safety cameras, including invoices, purchase orders, annual subscription payments, installation costs, and maintenance costs from the date of first installation through the present. Include any records showing federal, state, grant, or civil asset forfeiture funding used to offset costs. 
4. Camera Inventory and Placement The current inventory or deployment list of Flock Safety cameras operated by or accessible to this agency, including number of units and general location descriptions. Also include any written policies, criteria, risk assessments, or internal documents used to determine camera placement locations. 
5. Contracts and Legal Agreements Copies of all active and recently expired contracts, amendments, renewals, data-sharing agreements, memoranda of understanding, and scope-of-work documents between this agency and Flock Safety. 
6. Data Access and Network Sharing (a) The Flock "Organization Audit" report showing all searches made within this agency's Flock system from the date of installation through the date of this request. (b) The Flock "Network Audit" report showing all searches of this agency's Flock data by any outside agency from the date of installation through the date of this request. (c) A list of all agencies currently authorized to access this agency's Flock data, including any federal agencies. Please provide these records in their original electronic, machine-readable format (CSV or spreadsheet). 
7. Security Incidents and Unauthorized Access All records documenting any security incidents, unauthorized access, data breaches, hacking events, or unauthorized sharing of data collected by Flock Safety cameras, including any correspondence with or notifications from Flock Safety related to such incidents. 
8. Secretary of State Audit All records, correspondence, or internal communications related to the Illinois Secretary of State's 2025 audit of ALPR data-sharing practices, including any communications with the Secretary of State's office or Flock Safety regarding compliance. 
9. Marketing and Sales Materials All promotional, descriptive, and marketing materials shared with this agency by Flock Safety or any representative thereof prior to or in connection with the purchase or renewal of the Flock Safety system. 
10. Communications with Flock Safety Emails to/from Flock Safety personnel addresses; sales@flocksafety.com, support@flocksafety.com, or any email addresses in the format firstname.lastname@flocksafety.com from January 1, 2022 through the date this request is processed. title: California Public Records Act Request — Flock Safety ALPR Audit Logs

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: California Public Records Act Request — Flock Safety ALPR Audit Logs
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Under the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the audit logs, search logs, and usage reports associated with the Monterey Park Police Department's operation of Flock Safety Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) systems.

The records I seek were generated between September 5, 2025 and September 5, 2026, and consist of the following:

1. Organization Audit Logs (Search Logs) — a record of every license plate and vehicle-characteristic query run by department personnel in the Flock platform, including:

the date and time of each search;
the identity of the user who ran it (user ID, badge number, or name);
the query terms entered (plate numbers or vehicle descriptors);
any case number, reason, or justification recorded alongside the search.

2. Network Sharing Records — a current export or listing of the department's network share configuration, identifying both the outside agencies that receive Flock data from your department and the outside agencies whose data your department can access.


These records originate in a database and exist natively as structured data. I therefore ask that they be produced in that native electronic form — .CSV, .XLSX, or an equivalent spreadsheet file — consistent with Gov. Code § 7922.570(a). Please do not flatten the spreadsheets into PDFs.

To be clear, this request does not cover ALPR photographs, plate images, or investigative case files. It is limited to the administrative audit and usage records showing how department personnel have used the software.

If fees apply to the search or duplication of these records, please notify me before the total exceeds $20. I also request a waiver of all fees, as release of this information serves the public interest.

Should you conclude that any portion of the requested material is exempt, please issue a written response identifying the specific statutory exemption claimed, redact only the exempt portions, and release the balance of the records.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

LARECS

title: Nebraska Public Records Request — Lincoln/Lancaster ALPR Reports and Correspondence — 2018–Present

communications.subject: Nebraska Public Records Act Request: Nebraska Public Records Request — Lincoln/Lancaster ALPR Reports and Correspondence — 2018–Present
communications.communication:
Dear Nebraska Crime Commission Records Custodian:

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 84-712 through 84-712.09, I request copies of the following existing records held by the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice, also known as the Nebraska Crime Commission.

This request concerns annual reports and associated records submitted under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3206 regarding automatic license plate reader or automated license plate reader systems.

Please provide, for the period January 1, 2018 through the date this request is processed:

Every ALPR/LPR report, report form, attachment, supplement, correction, resubmission, or supporting document submitted to the Commission by:

Lincoln Police Department;

Lancaster County Sheriff’s Office;

Lancaster County;

Any other governmental entity located in Lincoln or Lancaster County that submitted an ALPR/LPR report to the Commission.

All correspondence between the Commission and any of those entities concerning ALPR/LPR reporting, including submission acknowledgments, reminders, late-report notices, deficiency notices, corrections, questions, compliance inquiries, and responses.

All records identifying entities that were required or expected to submit ALPR/LPR reports for the requested period, including reporting rosters, tracking spreadsheets, compliance lists, submission logs, or other records showing whether Lincoln Police Department, Lancaster County Sheriff’s Office, Lancaster County, or any other Lincoln/Lancaster governmental entity filed reports.

All Commission-issued instructions, templates, guidance, data dictionaries, policy guidance, training materials, interpretation memoranda, or reporting requirements relating to Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3206 and ALPR/LPR reporting.

Any aggregate statewide or regional ALPR/LPR reports, analysis, summaries, presentations, audits, or compliance reviews that include data for Lincoln, Lancaster County, Lincoln Police Department, Lancaster County Sheriff’s Office, or other governmental entities in Lancaster County.

All records reflecting the Commission’s treatment, review, storage, publication, or disclosure of § 60-3206 reports, including any determinations concerning confidentiality, redaction, or public availability.

I am not requesting raw captured license-plate data, individual license plate numbers, raw images, or other material excluded by Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3209. If any responsive records contain exempt content, please redact only the exempt information and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.

title: Laurence Lane Arnold

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Laurence Lane Arnold
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- The personnel file for Laurence Lane Arnold, my grandfather, born 1916, deceased 2003.
- Records for investigations or operations that he was assigned to when he was in the FBI, approximately 1941-1946.

Here is his find a grave and obituary to prove that he is deceased: https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/50078079/laurence-lane-arnold, https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/herald-review/name/laurence-arnold-obituary?id=51316855.

My grandfather served in the FBI during WWII, approximately 1941-1946. He was born in Newton IL, and died in Boise ID. During his time in the FBI, he was involved in operations in South America, likely the FBI's work countering operation Bolivar. He left the FBI after the war, so all responsive documents should be from this 5 range span.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. This is also to include any responsive records held in offsite locations, such as the Alexandria Records Center. Please include both investigatory and non-investigatory records in your search. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips, NARA file designations, as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Lena Bohman

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: CAM monitoring and evaluation plan
communications.communication:
To the FOIA Coordinator,

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, MCL 15.231 et seq., I am requesting records related to the Coordinated Assessment Model (CAM) monitoring and evaluation process referenced in the report titled "Strategic System Improvement Plan for Detroit’s Homelessness Response System, 2024-2028."

Please provide:

- Any CAM monitoring and evaluation plan, framework, protocol or similar document developed or used to assess the performance of CAM and Detroit’s coordinated entry system.
- Any completed monitoring reports, evaluation reports, scorecards, dashboards, summaries or findings produced pursuant to that plan from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request.
- Any implementation schedule, work plan or status document showing whether the CAM monitoring and evaluation activities identified in the Strategic System Improvement Plan have been completed, are ongoing or remain pending.

If any responsive records are maintained by or shared with the Homeless Action Network of Detroit (HAND) but are also in the City’s possession, custody or control, please include those records.

If any portion of a responsive record is exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt material, release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions, and cite the specific statutory exemption relied upon.

Please provide records electronically where available.

I request a waiver or reduction of fees because disclosure will contribute to public understanding of the performance and oversight of Detroit’s publicly supported homelessness response system and is not being sought for commercial purposes.

Thank you,
Aaron Mondry

title: Flock/Axon HECVAT responses (The Ohio State University)

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Flock/Axon HECVAT responses (The Ohio State University)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) questionnaire, in any version (Lite, Full, On-Premise, or numbered 2.x, 3.x, or 4.x), completed by or on behalf of Flock Group Inc. d/b/a Flock Safety and held by this institution, whether received from the vendor directly or downloaded from the EDUCAUSE Community Broker Index or another repository. This includes any HECVAT covering, by any name, Flock's Falcon license plate reader cameras, Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Raven audio/gunshot detection, Condor video cameras, or Flock drone / drone-as-first-responder services (including Aerodome).
2. Any HECVAT questionnaire, in any version, completed by or on behalf of Axon Enterprise, Inc. and held by this institution, on the same terms. This includes any HECVAT covering, by any name, Axon Outpost, Fusus (Axon Fusus / Fusus ONE / Real-Time Crime Center), Axon Evidence (Evidence.com), Axon Body cameras, Axon Fleet in-car systems including Fleet ALPR, Axon Respond, Axon Records, Axon Air, Axon Standards, or Axon Investigate.

HECVATs are generally completed per product or solution, so a vendor may have submitted more than one; I request all of them. If no HECVAT exists for a vendor or product, please say so rather than treating the item as a nil response for the vendor as a whole.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

HCvP

title: EO 14399 Voter Data Request (California Secretary of State - Election Division)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: EO 14399 Voter Data Request (California Secretary of State - Election Division)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All communications, letters, demands, instructions, and emails between United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (“USCIS”) agency officials, including but not limited to the USCIS’s Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (“FDNS”), and state election officials regarding:
-- The implementation of Executive Order 14399 (“Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections”).
-- Development of a state citizenship list portal, including any records, including drafts, attachments, and implementing guidance, concerning the USCIS “Executive Order 14399 Implementation” memoranda directing the creation of infrastructure for state citizenship portals (June 8, 2026), https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053/gov.uscourts.dcd.291053.151.1.pdf. 
-- Plans to transfer personally identifiable data to create state citizenship lists, including receipts showing data transfer between relevant agencies.
-- Implementation of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.” The “Unlawful Voter Initiative” refers to the initiative described in the “Disclosure Letter to Senator Padilla from Anonymous Whistleblower re: Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Direction to Identify ‘Unlawful Voters,’” (Sept 13, 2026), https://www.democrats.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/091326_-_senate_whistleblower_letter_dhs_uscis_combined_signedpdf.pdf. 

2) All memoranda of understanding (MOUs), data sharing agreements, or negotiations between state election officials and USCIS officials regarding granting federal agents access to personally identifiable data of state voters or the “Unlawful Voter Initiative.”

3) All log files, export or query counts, and metadata showing access of state voter data by USCIS personnel in searchable, machine-readable format, involving: time stamps, access metrics, confirmations of attestation statements (that the searcher is the voter or acting with the voter’s express authorization), search query parameters, pseudonymized user IDs, and system event codes. Remove personally identifiable information. 

4) Any internal complaints, alerts, incident investigations, audits, communications, reports, or notices regarding suspected violations of state election privacy laws relevant to the implementation of Executive Order 14399, the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” and the creation of state citizenship lists. 

I am requesting these records for the time period of March 1, 2026 to the present.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michelle Du

communications.communication:
Hello,

The SD-LECC is in receipt of your request dated and received on August 11, 2026, requesting records pursuant to the California Public Records Act (CPRA).  Preliminarily, it must be stated that the SD-LECC is not a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act.  It is a work location staffed with personnel from multiple local, state, and federal agencies working towards common operating goals, akin to a law enforcement "task force."  While a task force may, under certain circumstances, be considered a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act and the Brown Act, those circumstances do not exist with regard to the SD-LECC.  Nevertheless, the SD-LECC, in the spirit of public disclosure and openness, is responding to the request as if the SD-LECC were a self-contained, distinct public agency. The SD-LECC will provide you with responsive documents by end of business on August 20, 2026, and if any records are withheld, applicable exemptions will be identified at that time.

Thank you,


Roy W. Frank

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Texas Public Information Act, Tex. Gov't Code Chapter 552, I request copies of the following records held by this office, in any format (email and all attachments thereto, letters, memoranda, text messages, meeting calendars or logs, call logs, or notes):

- All communications, in either direction, between this office and any of the following individuals or organizations, regarding S.R. 438 (2009), S.B. 1634 (2025), or Lipan Apache tribal recognition generally, INCLUDING ALL ATTACHMENTS to any such communication (PDFs, scanned documents, images, or any other file type):

          - Individuals: Bernard F. Barcena Jr., Robert Soto, Lucille Contreras, Daniel Castro Romero Jr., Richard A. Gonzalez, Mandy/Mande Gonzales Davalos, Christina Hernandez, Margo Tamez, Eloisa Garcia Tamez, or any staff/representative acting on their behalf
          - Organizations: Lipan Apache Tribe of Texas, Lipan Apache Band of Texas, Texas Tribal Buffalo Project, Lipan Apache Tribe of Brackettville Texas, Lipan Apache Women Defense / LAW Defense, People of La Junta for Preservation
          - Any email address ending in: @lipanapachetribe.gov, @lipanapachetribe.org, @texastribalbuffaloproject.org, @lipanapachetribeofbrackettvilletexas.org, or @peopleoflajunta.org

- All records reflecting any meeting, call, or in-person contact between this office and any of the individuals or organizations listed above, including calendar entries, visitor logs, or scheduling records.

- Any documents, exhibits, proof of tribal status, genealogical records, organizational filings (articles of incorporation, IRS determination letters, bylaws), letters of support, or other supporting materials submitted to this office by any of the individuals or organizations listed above — whether submitted by email, mail, in person, or through any other channel, and whether or not attached to a specific tracked communication.

- Any internal memoranda, staff analysis, or briefing materials prepared regarding S.R. 438 or S.B. 1634, excluding only material specifically exempted as a draft or working paper under § 552.106.

Requested date range: March 1, 2009 through present.

I recognize this office may consider withholding certain records under Tex. Gov't Code §§ 306.003–306.004. State recognition of a tribe carries direct federal consequences under existing law, including the U.S. Small Business Administration's 8(a) Business Development program, which applies the label of "socially disadvantaged" status to enrolled members of state-recognized tribes, and the Indian Arts and Crafts Act of 1990 (18 U.S.C. § 1159), which governs who may lawfully market goods as authentic Native American-made. A separate GAO report (GAO-12-348, 2012) specifically points to federal funding the Lipan Apache have already received. As a reporter, this is a matter of genuine public interest under § 306.004(a)(3), not merely a private legislative matter.

I am requesting these records be produced in electronic format where available. If any portion of this request is denied or withheld, please cite the specific statutory exception relied upon for each withheld item, consistent with § 552.301. If costs are expected to exceed $40, please provide a written cost estimate before proceeding, per my rights under the Act.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tristan Ahtone

Dear Matthew Petti: 
This notice acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) received on 07/23/2020.     Please use the following unique FOIA tracking number CBP-2020-067978 to track the status of your request.  If you have not already done so, you must create a FOIAonline account at https://foiaonline.gov.  This is the only method available to check the status of your pending FOIA request. (https://foiaonline.regulations.gov/) 
Provisions of the Act allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS FOIA regulations outlined on the DHS website, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/11/22/2016-28095/freedom-of-information-act-regulations. By submitting your request, you have agreed to pay up to $25.00 in applicable processing fees, if any fees associated with your request exceed this amount, CBP shall contact you; however, the first 100 pages are free. (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/11/22/2016-28095/freedom-of-information-act-regulations) 
Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request.  Consistent with 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, CBP processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt.  Although CBP’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period in certain circumstances pursuant to 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(c).  [As your request seeks documents that will require a thorough and wide-ranging search, CBP will invoke a 10-day extension for your request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(c). If you would like to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office.  We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner.] OR [As your request seeks a voluminous amount of separate and distinct records, CBP will invoke a 10-day extension for your request pursuant to  6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(c).  If you would like to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office.  We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner.] OR [As the subject matter of your request is of substantial interest to two or more components of CBP or of substantial interest to another agency, we will need to consult with those entities before we issue a final response.  Due to these unusual circumstances, CBP will invoke a 10-day extension for your request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(c). If you would like to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office.  We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner.] 
CBP’s FOIA Division is working hard to reduce the amount of time necessary to respond to FOIA requests.  We truly appreciate your continued patience. 
For additional information please consult CBP FOIA website please click on FOIA Act Resources or visit (http://www.cbp.gov/site-policy-notices/foia) http://www.cbp.gov/site-policy-notices/foia. (http://www.cbp.gov/site-policy-notices/foia) 
Sincerely, 
U.S. Customs and Border Protection

title: Request for Lexipol correspondence (Chico Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Request for Lexipol correspondence (Chico Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records, between the Department and the company Lexipol  (lexipol.com) or its representatives that contain any references to “military equipment” or “AB 481”, including documents, emails and attachments, texts, spreadsheets, recordings, memoranda, and other materials, from July 1, 2024 to the present. 

Records on the Department’s web site indicate that it has used Lexipol templates for at least some policies. 

To assist with the prompt release of responsive material, I ask that you make records available to me as you locate them, rather than waiting until all responsive records have been collected and copied.
 
This request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

John Lindsay-Poland

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request records (documents, emails and attachments, texts, spreadsheets, recordings) of the Department or its staff containing the following:

Correspondence, purchase orders or contracts between Lexipol Inc. and the Department since January 1, 2022, including attachments to emails, and any policy and report templates provided by Lexipol.

I am seeking to understand how Lexipol, through its templates, correspondence or other information guides and informs the Department’s policy, especially as regards military equipment policies or annual reports.

Should you have any questions or concerns regarding this request, please feel free to contact me directly via email at jlindsay-poland@afsc.org or phone at 510-282-8983.

John Lindsay-Poland

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DOD self-identified trans records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Reports, policy memos, forms, form responses, emails, text messages, separation documents and other records regarding active-duty and reserve forces service members who have been diagnosed with or “exhibit symptoms consistent with” gender dysphoria and identified themselves for voluntary separation. I request records both from the Department of Defense connected to the separations, guiding policy and their requirements under Executive Order 14183, as well as records regarding individual service members' self-identification and voluntary separation. 

I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

I request a complete waiver of all search and duplication fees. If my request for a waiver is denied, I request that I be considered a member of the news media for fee purposes. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, processed by a representative of the news media/press and is made in the process of news gathering and not for commercial usage. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Under the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, agencies must adopt a presumption of disclosure, withholding information “only if . . . disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption” or “disclosure is prohibited by law.”

The FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 also amended the FOIA as follows (5 USC 552(a)(8)):

(A) An agency shall—
(i) withhold information under this section only if—
(I) the agency reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption described in subsection (b); or
(II) disclosure is prohibited by law; and
(ii) (I) consider whether partial disclosure of information is possible whenever the agency determines that a full disclosure of a requested record is not possible; and
(II) take reasonable steps necessary to segregate and release nonexempt information. . .

In the event some portions of the requested records are properly exempt from disclosure, please disclose any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of the requested records. If it is your position that a document contains non-exempt segments, but that those non-exempt segments are so dispersed throughout the document as to make segregation impossible, please state what portion of the document is non-exempt, and how the material is dispersed throughout the document. Claims of nonsegregability must be made with the same degree of detail as required for claims of exemptions in a Vaughn index. If a request is denied in whole, please state specifically that it is not reasonable to segregate portions of the record for release.

Further, “the withholding agency must supply ‘a relatively detailed justification, specifically identifying the reasons why a particular exemption is relevant and correlating those claims with the particular part of a withheld document to which they apply.’”

In addition, I ask that your agency exercise its discretion to release records which may be technically exempt, but where withholding serves no important public interest.

If a portion of the responsive records become available before the entire request is complete, I respectfully request that the department provide records on a rolling basis.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ileana Garnand

title: Sacramento Sheriff Social Media Inquiry #2

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Sacramento Sheriff Social Media Inquiry #2
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All messages sent or received by Sacramento Sheriffs Office official instagram pages between January 1st, 2025 to June 27th 2025.

Original JPG. files, including the meta data, of all images posted on the Sacramento Sheriffs Instagram Profile between January 1st, 2025 to June 27th 2025.

All screenshots, taken by any agent of the Sacramento Sheriffs Department, that were posted onto Sacramento Sheriffs Office Instagram Page, on June 19th 2025.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

title: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data on breached account containing  MnCHOICES reports

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data on breached account containing  MnCHOICES reports
communications.communication:
Aitkin County Data Practices Compliance Official

Subject: MGDPA Request: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data

Statutory Framework and ADA Accommodation Request
Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (Minn. Stat. Chapter 13), I am requesting access to the public government data listed below.

Under Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. §§ 12131-12165) and the MGDPA, I have a statutory right to inspect this data at no charge. Due to the volume and technical complexity of the requested materials, an at-length, in-person inspection is not feasible without a customized environment. Therefore, as a reasonable accommodation, I request to inspect these records in their original electronic format via a secure remote connection.

To eliminate the administrative burden on your agency to facilitate a live remote inspection, I will accept digital copies of the requested records delivered via email at no cost. Delivery of these digital copies fully satisfies this ADA accommodation request.

There should be no charge for this request. If you determine Aitkin County would like to charge for this request beyond the cost of the storage medium, or if the cost of storage of the data segregated for inspection would exceed $50 (e.g., 2TB at commercial pricing), do not proceed without contacting me.

Data Requested
I am requesting the following strictly public administrative IT records regarding the environment surrounding the data security incident discovered on April 8, 2026:

Account Configuration: IT administrative records, provisioning logs, or server configurations indicating whether the compromised email account utilized to store the MnCHOICES report was assigned to a single individual user or configured as a shared distribution list/group inbox.

Retention Policies: The active Aitkin County Records Retention Schedule and Email Management Policy in effect during April 2026.

Parameters
This request explicitly excludes any Private Data on Individuals. I am requesting only the public IT configurations and administrative policies. If you determine any portion of this request encompasses classified data, you must provide the specific statutory citation authorizing the redaction or denial, as required by Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(f).

Appendix: Technical Search and Retrieval Parameters
To facilitate compliance and limit the administrative burden on your IT department, please route the following parameter to the Microsoft 365/Exchange Administrator:

For Item 1 (Account Configuration): Within the Exchange Admin Center (EAC), navigate to Recipients -> Mailboxes. Provide a screenshot or administrative export showing the RecipientTypeDetails (e.g., UserMailbox vs. SharedMailbox) for the specific account(s) compromised in the April 2026 breach. Alternatively, run the Exchange Online PowerShell cmdlet: Get-EXOMailbox -Identity <CompromisedAccountAddress> | Format-List Name, RecipientTypeDetails, ForwardingAddress and provide the textual output.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-exomailbox

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Jonathan Murray

communications.subject: RE: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Public IT Configuration and Policy Data on breached account containing  MnCHOICES reports
communications.communication:
On 9/10/2026 I sent an email reply to the other email address you were using of 217444-43950412@requests.muckrock.com<mailto:217444-43950412@requests.muckrock.com>



  *   I will paste that reply here:






Mr. Jonathon Murray,



Thank you for your patience and your questions. It’s our understanding that the DHS fields potentially affected were: FormID, an ID to designate the person, “personname,” a “PMI,” formtype, “type,” State, a modified date, last modified by (whom), org, and locations.



In terms of your other questions, they may be better directed to DHS. However, I do want you to know some additional information we have. Typically, DHS would pull and provide us our individual county data. In this instance, though we did not request it (or, frankly, know it was sent), DHS filtered the spreadsheet and sent the filtered version of the spreadsheet to us, but containing information from all 87 Counties. Upon receipt, with the filtering involved, the recipient at our county did not know there was other out-of-county information included. That email was deleted shortly after receipt. Only in the wake of this incident did a forensic analyst locate the filtered spreadsheet in the user’s Deleted items folder. We have since modified our settings as to Deleted Items folders. We have no evidence of any leak of any of this data. We have no evidence of any of this information being misused in any way.



I would also point out that, as noted in the letter you received from DHS, they stopped transmitting MnCHOICES data in June 2025, which was approximately a year before the incident.
